title: Access to Justice
question_text: Should it be easy or hard to take someone to court?

Reasonable standards that keep out frivolous cases without blocking legitimate ones.
Higher bars are fine. Too much litigation clogs the system and costs everyone money.

question_text: Should a judge trust what prosecutors say, or watch them closely?

stances.text: Watch closely. Prosecutors have enormous power and real incentives to win. A judge's job is to make sure that power is used fairly.
Be skeptical. Hold prosecution to strict standards — especially on evidence handling and plea deals.
Treat both sides equally and let the process work.

Making sure others think twice before doing the same thing.

title: Judicial & Prosecutorial Discretion
question_text: When government and a citizen clash, who gets the benefit of the doubt?

stances.text: The citizen, almost always. Government has lawyers, money, and power. Regular people need courts to level the playing field.
The citizen usually — unless the government has clear legal authority on its side.
Neither side automatically. Look at the facts and apply the law evenly.
The government usually — it represents everyone, and its decisions deserve respect unless clearly wrong.

title: Judicial Interpretation
question_text: Does the law change with the times, or does it mean what it said when it was written?

stances.text: Courts should reconsider old rulings when we know more or society has changed. Keeping bad precedent alive is its own injustice.

The law means what it says. Use original intent to fill gaps, but don't stretch the meaning.
